q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM ( SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(1) AS CNT FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY FROM CUSTOMER ) AS T GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID ) AS T2 WHERE T2.CNT=(SELECT COUNT(1) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM ( SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(1) AS CNT FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY FROM CUSTOMER ) AS T GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID ) AS T2 WHERE T2.CNT=(SELECT COUNT(1) FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (101, 1), (101, 2), (101, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct product keys they have purchased is equal to the total count of distinct product keys in the product table. Q2 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct product keys they have purchased is equal to the total count of products in the product table.
counterexample_dsp: A customer who has purchased all products in the product table.
